title: Microsoft Teams: external bot detection and activity reports in the Teams admin center
summary: The briefing correctly separates the planned report from the documented meeting policy, and its actionable path and command are supported. Two minor corrections should acknowledge disagreements between Microsoft's pages about the detection-disabled PowerShell value and general report access roles.

claims.claim: The existing bot control is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting join & lobby > Manage external bots and their access to meetings.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select Meetings > Meeting policies. Select the policy you want to modify, or create a new policy. Under Meeting join & lobby, find Manage external bots and their access to meetings.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ExternalBotAccessMode RequireApprovalWhenDetected configures the approval-required bot policy in the MicrosoftTeams module.
claims.quote: Module: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell module. -Identity: Specify the name of the policy being created. RequireApprovalWhenDetected: When detected, bots will be enforced to the meeting lobby, regardless of the lobby setting of the meeting.

claims.claim: The bot setting applies to meetings hosted by users assigned the meeting policy.
claims.quote: The setting applies to meetings hosted by users assigned the meeting policy.

claims.claim: The existing bot policy can be applied at user or group level.
claims.quote: Scope: Meetings policies at a user / group level

claims.claim: The bot management page gives AllowBots as the detection-disabled PowerShell value.
claims.quote: Do not detect bots | AllowBots | Bots aren't detected or marked in the lobby or in the meeting.
claims.fix: Remove 'AllowBots' from the unqualified 'Other values' note, leaving 'Other value: BlockDetectedBots.' After the sentence listing the bot management page's values, add: 'The Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy reference instead lists AllowAllBots for disabling detection; Microsoft's pages disagree on this value.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamsmeetingpolicy?view=teams-ps, whose ExternalBotAccessMode section says 'AllowAllBots: Don't detect bots'.

claims.claim: BlockDetectedBots is the PowerShell value for blocking detected bots.
claims.quote: BlockDetectedBots: When detected, external third-party meeting bots and meeting assistants are blocked from joining meetings hosted in the organization.
